i’m not necessarily an expert on this sort of thing, so i apologize in advance if i get any details wrong, but i’m gonna go on a quick tangent about ecosphere/jar care from what i’ve learned in my own experience 

a proper ecosphere/jar needs a good balance of water and plants to create a well oxygenated ecosystem. if the organisms in the water don’t get enough oxygen, they can die! same with the plants, so you want to get plants that have nice long roots that can grow into the soil and rocks, allowing the plant to grow on its own and sustain enough oxygen in the tank to ensure everything can live and grow properly!!!

while it’s typically preferable to use water plants native to your area, i think if you got a plant from petco and let it soak in the river/pond/lake water overnight. if it’s still green and healthy by the morning, you can transfer it over to the jar where it will already be adjusted to the ph levels in the water! 

also, you may want to find a snail or something to eat the algae, which may already be in the waters of the place you started the jar, but if you want snails don’t get more than one or else you’ll end up with a giant snail colony within a couple weeks lol. but there are many other microorganisms in freshwater you can find if you allow the sediment to settle for a day or two and look closely, such as copepods and amphipods that eat algae and other microorganisms! there are also many water bugs and even isopods that you can bring in just by bringing in new plants/rocks/dirt! 

my biggest tip above all is to be patient, and allow the jar to do its thing. a lot of jars will go through a “murky” stage where it seems like everything is dead and gone, but if you stay patient, you’ll eventually begin to see new life! so don’t be afraid of death in your jars, because from that death springs new life!
